description: Infiniti Oracle is the AI-native market intelligence layer for prediction markets. This feed publishes hourly briefings on Polymarket, Kalshi and beyond — major market movements, volume records, regulatory and legal developments, new notable markets, and high-signal political, economic and crypto predictions — plus live commodities and crypto stats blocks tracking gold, oil, natural gas and BTC/ETH/SOL price action.

items.title: Kalshi sports ban takes effect in Massachusetts today
items.summary: A judge's injunction blocking Kalshi's sports-event contracts goes into effect Friday; the court said Kalshi "mirrors other digital gambling experiences," and Kalshi is eligible to appeal .

items.title: Polymarket counter-sues Massachusetts in federal court
items.summary: Polymarket filed Monday in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts against AG Andrea Campbell and gaming officials, arguing the Commodity Exchange Act gives the CFTC exclusive jurisdiction over event contracts; CLO Neal Kumar: "Congress gave the CFTC, not states, exclusive authority over event contracts" .

items.title: Kalshi's 15-minute gold markets out-fee ether markets 2:1
items.summary: The short-duration gold contracts, launched weeks ago, generated nearly twice the trading fees of Kalshi's Ether-linked markets in September, with the live 15-min gold market showing $140,707 volume .

items.title: Traders trim year-end gold optimism as prices slide
items.summary: Gold at ~$4,312 is down >8% in a month; Kalshi traders now price gold finishing 2026 at $4,300+ at 60% (down from 72% earlier this month), $4,500 at ~31%, and $5,000 at just 12% .

items.title: Tennessee–Arkansas markets split on QB uncertainty
items.summary: No. 15 Vols priced 83% on both Polymarket and Kalshi to win Saturday, but Polymarket's first-quarter winner dropped 7 points on Tennessee while Kalshi's first-TD market dropped 7 points, as George MacIntyre is expected to start; Kalshi volume just $56,245 .

items.title: CNN: midterm "mention markets" fuel insider-trading alarms
items.summary: A new CNN investigation reports prediction sites now offer an average of 44 granular markets per race, and Kalshi has suspended at least six 2026 candidates this year for betting on their own races; the piece revisits the summer case of Trump's White House teleprompter operator settling an insider-trading probe for $65,000 over "mention markets" in Trump speeches. Kalshi's head of enforcement says screening for irregular activity is continuous; Polymarket hired a former FBI official and says it regularly refers cases to the DOJ .

items.title: Polymarket signs with the Rangers; NHL remains the only league aboard

The NHL is still the only major sports league formally partnered with prediction-market platforms; the NFL, MLB and NBA have stayed away while CNBC and CNN integrate market data .

items.title: Torres formally introduces insider-trading bill Friday, backed by Pelosi
items.summary: The Public Integrity in Financial Prediction Markets Act of 2026 was introduced with 30+ Democratic co-sponsors including former Speaker Nancy Pelosi, Rep. Andre Carson and Rep. Rashida Tlaib; it bars federal elected officials, appointees, executive staff and congressional aides from trading event contracts tied to government action when holding or able to reasonably obtain material nonpublic information. Torres: "all the hallmarks of potential insider trading." Kalshi says it already prohibits MNPI-based trading .

items.title: Senate version from Merkley/Klobuchar; Murphy bill coming too
items.summary: Sens. Merkley and Klobuchar's companion proposal would bar government officials from trading prediction markets and strengthen the CFTC's power to go after bad actors, citing the ~$400k Maduro-contract win and similar suspect Iran-linked trades; last month Israeli authorities brought securities charges over Polymarket trades on Iran military actions. Sen. Murphy (D-CT) plans his own bill this month targeting "mention" markets on government actions, while leaving economic derivatives untouched .

items.title: Federal judge blocks Minnesota's prediction markets ban
items.summary: Judge Menendez granted a preliminary injunction, finding the state's statute likely at least partially preempted by the CEA since the CFTC has exclusive jurisdiction over swaps traded on DCMs; infringement on that authority is itself irreparable harm. The ruling landed the same day Kalshi agreed with the Nevada Gaming Control Board to add third-party geofencing for Nevada users .

items.title: Polymarket sues Massachusetts over crackdown
items.summary: Polymarket filed in federal court against AG Andrea Campbell, arguing "Congress gave the CFTC, not states, exclusive authority over event contracts" and seeking to block state gambling-law enforcement. The suit cites the Feb. 6 injunction Massachusetts won against Kalshi that ordered it to drop sports-event contracts within 30 days without a state license .

items.title: Canada approves Wealthsimple prediction markets — sports and politics excluded
items.summary: The Canadian Investment Regulatory Organization cleared Wealthsimple to offer event contracts on economic forecasts (labor, housing, central-bank rates, environment, financial indicators), but drew a hard line: no "yes/no" contracts on political or sporting events. Other provinces can still refuse authorization .

items.title: NHL deepens ties: Rangers partner with Polymarket
items.summary: Two weeks after the Kalshi–Blackhawks deal (the first with a North American pro team), MSG Sports announced a Polymarket partnership covering the Rangers only, not the Knicks. The NHL remains the only major league to embrace prediction markets — Bettman says it "gives us control" to force takedowns of contracts the league deems inappropriate — while the NFL, MLB and NBA stay away .

items.title: Baltimore sues Kalshi and Polymarket
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Scott and the City Council filed suits Thursday under the city's Consumer Protection Ordinance, accusing both companies of running illegal, unlicensed sports betting and misleading consumers about the legality and regulatory status of their products .

items.title: Seminole Tribe sues DraftKings and CEO Jason Robins
items.summary: The tribe holding Florida's sports-betting monopoly wants a Broward County court to shut down DraftKings' prediction-market sports tab and its Pick6 game, and accuses Robins personally of racketeering. The tribe is suing under state law in state court, where DraftKings' federal preemption defense has to be won rather than assumed .

items.title: $3M+ spent on influence in 2026
items.summary: OpenSecrets: Kalshi, Polymarket and the Coalition for Prediction Markets spent at least $3 million on lobbying and campaign contributions at federal and state levels this year. Kalshi has hired at least one lobbyist in 41 states — every state that has introduced prediction-market-specific legislation .

items.title: Gold micro-markets out-earning ether on Kalshi
items.summary: Kalshi's 15-minute gold contracts generated nearly twice the trading fees of ether-linked markets in September, only weeks after launching; short-duration commodity contracts are attracting the heaviest flow .

items.title: UK door stays half-closed
items.summary: FCA markets chief Simon Walls confirmed Oct. 6 that the regulator is in talks with prediction-market operators about UK entry, but the retail binary-options ban in force since 2019 still blocks financial prediction products; sports and political markets would need separate gambling licenses .

CFTC fires back at the NFL: league declined cooperation MOU
items.summary: After the NFL's amicus brief urging SCOTUS to review the Kalshi case, the CFTC said "it's unfortunate the NFL declined to sign an MOU" that would let the league share information and cooperate on market integrity. Kalshi's response to New Jersey's petition is due Nov. 9; the Court isn't expected to decide on review before December .

items.title: NFL's numbers: $1.8B of $3.3B on NFL Sunday, and no 21+ floor
items.summary: The league says nearly $2B of first-Sunday volume was NFL-tied, the CFTC has just 543 staff nationwide, and neither the agency nor platforms have banned easily-manipulated contracts or set a 21 age minimum — Kalshi allows trading at 18, traditional books require 21 .
